notes:
Top-line: Temposphere runs a real-time personalization and bidding stack for programmatic ad placement. Super latency- and cost-sensitive — business driver is CPM uplift versus inference spend. Looking for Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quantization) and a quantitative perf benchmark before commit.

Key quotes from CTO: 'We need 95th/99th p99 tail visibility at production load; can't accept >50ms P99 for 32-token scoring on critical path.'

Technical summary / asks: want a short perf run comparing: hosted small-scale (g6-like), Dedicated with reserved GPU pools (A100/80GB equiv), and quantized int8 variants. Specific metrics requested: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (qps) at 90% SLO, CPU/GPU utilization, per-token cost, and batching impact curve (batch size vs latency/cost). Also need KV/prefix caching numbers: cache hit rate vs cost savings and cold-start latencies.

Cost sensitivity: targeted average unit cost <$0.0009/token for inference on reranking flows (200–400M infer tokens/month). If caching/batching can reduce cost by 20–35% without increasing tail latency, higher preference for Dedicated.

Security/compliance: must support SSO/SAML, KMS-managed keys for dataset encryption, audit logs, and EU data residency flag for specific customers. Legal requested Redwood's SOC2 report and a short security FAQ.

Sales pitch notes: Temposphere already evaluated Replicate and OpenAI endpoints for latency but saw inconsistent p99 under load; interested in Redwood's automatic batching/caching and quantization guidance. Wants concrete runbook: config knobs, suggested batch windows, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles per model size.

PRIORITY: Perf benchmark + POC scope by 2026-03-20. AE to secure pricing band and Dedicated sizing.
